Our platform provider will perform routine maintenance to our database cluster on Tuesday, 20th October 2026 during our agreed maintenance window of 09:00 - 13:00 UTC.

**We do not anticipate any substantial downtime**. However, the management UI and REST API may be interrupted briefly during the window.

Whilst maintenance windows are 4 hours long, our provider attempts to begin the maintenance as close to the beginning of the window as possible, the maintenance itself usually only takes 10-60 seconds to complete.

We will provide updates in this notice as the maintenance progresses.
The maintenance is now complete. Thanks for your patience.
The maintenance has now been completed. We’ve double-checked everything and can confirm that all services are working just as they should. Thanks for your patience!

We’ve fixed an issue that could prevent a status page from being deleted if a team member had previously collapsed or dismissed its getting-started checklist.

Affected pages can now be deleted as expected.

You can now archive past notices manually, without waiting for your automatic archive settings to take effect. This gives you more control over your status-page history without deleting the original notices.

Choose Archive Notice from a notice’s actions menu, either in the notice list or when editing it. Archived notices stay in their usual position in your dashboard, clearly marked, so they’re easy to find again.

You can also choose Unarchive Notice to restore a notice to your status-page history - including notices that were archived automatically.

Your existing automatic archiving continues to work as before - there’s nothing new to configure.

notices.subject: Fixed: Notification delivery across enabled channels

latest_update.content:
We’ve fixed an issue where subscribers with a deactivated email address could be excluded from status updates entirely, even when they had another notification channel enabled.

Updates will now continue through their other eligible channels, while delivery to the deactivated email address remains suppressed. Existing channel and Component preferences continue to apply.

No action is needed.

We’ve fixed a bug where the fallback text for some Slack notifications could include a subscriber-specific Access Link, even though the visible message used the public status page link. Both parts of the notification now use the same public link.

notices.subject: Fixed: Maintenance message missing from the Status API

latest_update.content:
We’ve resolved a bug that caused the Status API’s state_text field to return null while a status page was under maintenance, even when a custom maintenance message had been configured.

The API now returns the configured maintenance message as expected, consistent with operational and degraded states. No changes are needed to existing integrations.
The maintenance is now complete. Thanks for your patience.

notices.subject: Finalised our Ruby on Rails platform upgrade

latest_update.content:
We’ve completed the final stage of our recent Ruby on Rails platform upgrade. Following a careful rollout and monitoring period, all parts of the upgrade are now active in production and performing normally.

This work strengthens the foundations of Sorry and prepares the platform for further improvements. No action is required from customers.

notices.subject: Upgraded our Ruby on Rails platform

latest_update.content:
Today we completed an upgrade of the Ruby on Rails framework that powers Sorry™.

This is a behind-the-scenes change with no intended visible impact for customers. Before switching production traffic, we ran our automated test suite against both framework versions, completed manual QA in staging, and monitored the upgrade under live production traffic. Performance and error rates have remained normal.

Completing this work provides a stronger foundation for future platform improvements, allowing us to adopt newer framework capabilities through smaller, safer upgrades.

notices.subject: A little speed boost for public status pages

latest_update.content: We’ve made a handful of behind-the-scenes improvements to help public status pages load more quickly, with the biggest gains on pages with a long notice history. There’s nothing you need to do and no change to how your page looks or works — it should simply feel a little snappier.

We’ve made another small batch of improvements to how status page metrics and uptime are calculated.

There’s nothing you need to do, but it gives us a sturdier foundation for future updates while helping status pages remain accurate and responsive.

notices.subject: Keeping status pages secure and up to date

latest_update.content: We’ve updated some of the underlying technology that powers public status pages, keeping it aligned with current security and maintenance standards. It’s a behind-the-scenes improvement, so there’s nothing you need to do and no change to how your status page looks or works.

notices.subject: A little more status page groundwork

latest_update.content:
We’ve rolled out another set of behind-the-scenes improvements to how status pages work out their current status and choose which recent notices to display.

You shouldn’t notice any big changes just yet, but it gives us a tidier foundation for some improvements we’re working towards. We’ve also been keeping a close eye on performance throughout, and everything is looking nice and steady.

We’ve improved how public status pages are presented to search engines. Large pages with lots of components or a long notice history now use smaller, more focused sitemaps, making them faster and more reliable to process.

We’ve also refined which content is included, prioritising the most useful public pages and adding the Status API guide. There’s nothing you need to do—these improvements will be applied automatically.

notices.subject: A little groundwork for future improvements

latest_update.content:
We’ve shipped a few behind-the-scenes changes to prepare status pages for some future improvements.

Along the way, we’ve expanded our automated performance checks to cover larger, busier pages and more real-world scenarios. This should help us spot potential slowdowns earlier and keep status pages running smoothly as we continue to build.

There’s nothing you need to do — it’s simply some useful groundwork for what’s coming next.

notices.subject: Status API improvements for private pages

latest_update.content:
We’ve given the Status API a bit of a tidy-up. Most importantly, it now works properly with private status pages, so you can securely use the API without making your page public.

We’ve also refreshed the API documentation with clearer, copy-and-paste cURL examples and a few visual tweaks to make everything easier to follow.

If you have a private status page, sign in and visit its API page to find your authentication details and updated examples. Existing API integrations will continue working as before.
We’ve simplified the way components load on status pages. It’s a behind-the-scenes improvement, so there’s nothing you need to do and no change to how your status page works.

notices.subject: Fixed: Some team members unable to reorder components

latest_update.content: We resolved a bug that prevented some team members with restricted page access from saving changes when reordering components. Instead of applying the new order, the page displayed an error and left the components unchanged. Component reordering now works as expected for all team members with permission to manage the page.

Our monitoring has shown the service to be stable over the past 30 minutes, and the Help Centre remains fully available.

We appreciate your patience while this issue was being investigated and resolved.

notices.subject: Your subscribers stay in the loop, even as your components evolve

latest_update.content:
We've made an improvement that keeps subscriber notifications accurate whenever you add or move components on your status page.

As you reorganise things over time, these changes could previously leave a subscriber's notification preferences slightly out of step with your new structure. Now we automatically keep everyone aligned with your latest layout, so they keep hearing about exactly the things they care about, and nothing they don't.

**What this means for you and your subscribers**

- **Add a Subcomponent:** anyone already following the parent automatically starts receiving updates about the newly added subcomponent.
- **Move a Component:** subscribers keep receiving updates for whatever they initially chose to follow, wherever it now sits in your component structure.

And if you delete a component, there's nothing to worry about — subscribers stay on your list and simply stop hearing about the part you removed.

**Do I need to do anything?**

No. This works automatically across your status pages, including changes made through the dashboard, the API, and when importing from another provider. Your subscribers' existing choices are always respected.
